1. In `Book::Release.finalize_release`, `Book.find(id)` loads one `Book` instance and `ReleaseMarker.for(id)` loads a second, separate `Book` instance for the same row before the transaction starts. Inside the transaction, the first instance updates `title`/`subtitle` while the second instance (still holding the old working `title` in memory) updates `published: true`. When the transaction commits, ActiveRecord deduplicates commit callback targets by record identity and runs `after_update_commit :write_recap` only on the last saved instance (`ReleaseMarker`'s `@book`), writing `{ title: old_working_title, published: true }` into `Rails.cache`.
2. Furthermore, `Book::Recap#write_recap` reads in-memory `title` and `published`, which makes it vulnerable whenever multiple in-memory instances of the same `Book` are updated or touched (e.g., via `Leaf`'s `belongs_to :book, touch: true`) within a transaction.

Let's fix both `app/models/book/release.rb` (updating a single `Book` instance atomically) and `app/models/book/recap.rb` (reading committed `title` and `published` from the database in `write_recap` without mutating `self`).

The `after_update_commit` callback will correctly execute after the transaction. We should, however, make sure to leave the `ReleaseMarker` class intact to avoid any breaking changes for other code that might rely on it directly.

Next, onto `Book::Recap`. The `write_recap` method uses an `after_update_commit` callback to cache information about a book. I'm scrutinizing every detail here, starting with the cache store. If it's `:memory_store` or `:redis_cache_store`, the method correctly writes the book's title and published status to the cache using the book's ID as a key.

There's no chance of overwriting the values of different books, as each book will have a unique cache key based on its ID. The `after_update_commit` callback guarantees the cache writes are always current and not stale. If a transaction rolls back, the callback never fires, leaving the cache untouched. module Book::Release
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  class_methods do
    def finalize_release(id, title:, subtitle: nil)
      book = find(id)
      return false if book.published?

      book.update! title: title, subtitle: subtitle || book.subtitle, published: true

      true
    end
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/book/recap.rb
module Book::Recap
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_update_commit :write_recap
  end

  def cached_recap
    Rails.cache.read(recap_cache_key)
  end

  def recap_cache_key
    [ "book_recap", id ]
  end

  private
    def write_recap
      values = self.class.uncached { self.class.where(id: id).pick(:title, :published) }
      return unless values

      current_title, current_published = values
      Rails.cache.write recap_cache_key,
        { title: current_title, published: current_published },
        expires_in: Rails.application.config.x.recap.expires_in
    end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class Books::ReleasesControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @original_cache = Rails.cache

  end

    assert_response :forbidden

  end

    assert_response :success

    end
  end
